title: Interpretation Rules (Tier 2)
description: Schema for the Tier-2 signal-mapping config that translates descriptive evidence labels emitted by cards into per-modality signals consumed by the Tier-3 synthesis layer. Consolidates normative knowledge that previously lived scattered across (a) card_spec interpretation_hints[].dominant flags, (b) modality-module killer_conditions, and (c) the synthesis-layer NOT_INFORMATIVE_CALLS set. Reviewable by domain experts in PR; version-controlled with the contracts.

axis.description: The biology axis this rules file applies to (e.g. intracellular_intrinsic, surface_intrinsic). Matches the dashboard_spec's axis_resolution outputs.

rules.description: Ordered list of evidence→signal mappings. Each rule fires when its predicate matches a card's emitted descriptive label; emits a per-modality signal vector. Multiple matching rules accumulate signals.

rationale.description: Optional free-text explanation of the rules file's design intent (audience: future biology reviewers).

signal_vocabulary.description: Controlled signal vocabulary. 'supportive' = evidence consistent with this modality. 'opposing' = evidence against. 'killer' = hard gate to not_viable (Tier-3 deterministic). 'neutral' = informational, no fit-level effect. 'insufficient' = data missing/uninformative; counts toward coverage gap.

rule_id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this rule. Surfaced in provenance for audit ('this signal came from rule X').

when.description: Predicate that matches the rule against a card's emitted descriptive label. The card_id + field together identify which summary_field on which card to inspect; equals/in selects matching values.

field.description: The summary_field on the card to inspect (e.g. 'dependency_class', 'selectivity_class', 'correlation_class').

signals.description: Map of modality_id → signal_vocabulary. Each rule emits a signal for each listed modality. Modalities not listed receive 'neutral'.

dominant.description: If true AND signal == supportive for a given modality, this is treated as a DOMINANT positive signal in Tier-3 EG4 scoring (one dominant signal + non-contradiction is sufficient for 'strong' fit). Mirrors today's interpretation_hints[].dominant semantics but now lives in the rules layer.

killer_message.description: Stakeholder-readable rationale shown when this rule fires a 'killer' signal. Required for rules emitting any killer signal; ignored otherwise. Surfaces in the dashboard's modality-fit narrative.

rationale.description: Optional biology explanation of why this evidence→signal mapping holds. Free text; for PR review.
